headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: ComfyUI is offline/local, while the zoomcamp is non-runnable, so pairwise interaction is mostly absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline by default and has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, or MCP bridge; the zoomcamp is non-runnable and exposes no runtime channel. With no shared communication path, there is no plausible prompt-injection route between agent_a and agent_b.
conditions: IF agent_a is connected to agent_b through a shared filesystem, clipboard, or queue not shown in the profiles, reassess upward.
IF agent_b is converted into a runnable agent that ingests agent_a outputs, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or message queues.
Do not add an MCP bridge between the two agents.
Review any future orchestrator for provenance tagging.
requires-engineering: add explicit trust boundaries if a shared workspace is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches image/model assets and can call a vendor API, but its profile says it works fully offline unless configured otherwise; agent_b has no I/O surfaces and is non-runnable. Leakage is therefore limited unless an operator introduces a shared workspace or external upload path.
conditions: IF agent_a is configured to upload prompts, images, or model artifacts to a third-party service, reassess upward.
IF agent_b is given access to the same workspace or files as agent_a, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep sensitive images and checkpoints off shared storage.
Disable any optional cloud/API upload path.
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and agent_b is not runnable and has no write scopes. There is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory or git repo, reassess upward.
IF agent_b becomes runnable with mutable resource access, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only relative to shared repos.
Avoid mounting the same writable volume into both agents.
Document any future shared state as single-writer.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate outputs that a human may use in workflows, but agent_b is a course repository and not a decision-making agent, so there is no documented automation chain where B acts on A's outputs. Any cascade would require unusual orchestration outside the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is wrapped in automation that consumes agent_a outputs as authoritative inputs, reassess upward.
IF agent_a outputs are directly copied into downstream actions without review, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before reusing generated outputs.
Do not auto-ingest agent_a outputs into downstream pipelines.
Label generated content as unverified.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any action-taking step.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: agent_a is an offline open-source image tool with no declared sensitive-data residency, and agent_b is a non-runnable course repository with no data classes touched. The profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or retention differences.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data classes not listed here, reassess compliance.
IF residency or retention policies are added that differ across the pair, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data into either agent.
Record any future retention policy before deployment.
Keep the course repo separate from production data.
requires-engineering: add a compliance review if regulated data is introduced.
